# Sweep

> A free, open-source Chrome extension that finds every email from one sender in Gmail and
> selects them all, so they can be deleted in two clicks. It makes no network requests, has
> no server, and never asks for Google account access.

Sweep adds a "Similar" button to Gmail's conversation toolbar. It reads the sender of the
open message, searches for that sender, waits for the results, and applies Gmail's "select
all conversations that match this search" step automatically. The user then presses Gmail's
own Delete button, so deleted mail goes to Trash and stays recoverable for 30 days.

Unlike inbox-cleaning services, Sweep does not use the Gmail API and requests no OAuth
access. It operates only on the Gmail page already open in the browser. Its single Chrome
permission is `storage`, used to remember filter preferences locally.

It also adds a second pagination control at the bottom of Gmail's message lists, which
Gmail only provides at the top.

## Pages

- [Home](https://pekhota.github.io/sweep-for-gmail/): what it does, how it works, privacy comparison
- [How to delete all emails from one sender in Gmail](https://pekhota.github.io/sweep-for-gmail/delete-all-emails-from-one-sender-in-gmail/): complete manual method, Gmail search operators, storage guidance
- [Privacy policy](https://pekhota.github.io/sweep-for-gmail/privacy.html): full data-use statement
- [Source code](https://github.com/pekhota/sweep-for-gmail): MIT licensed, one readable file, no build step

## Facts

- Price: free, no paid tier, no subscription
- Licence: MIT
- Data collected: none
- Network requests: none
- Chrome permissions: `storage` only
- Works on: mail.google.com in Chrome-based browsers
- Does not support: Gmail's basic HTML view
